title: Board-approved IT strategy and governance framework
summary: An IT governance framework covers strategic alignment, risk, resource and performance management and BCP/DR with defined Board and senior-management roles; the Board approves IT strategy and policies and reviews them annually.
typical_evidence: Board-approved IT strategy and governance framework; Board minutes
category: RBI IT Governance MD 2023 (now 2026 cyber directions): paras 4-5

title: IT Strategy Committee of the Board
summary: A Board IT Strategy Committee of at least three directors, chaired by an independent director with IT expertise, meets at least quarterly and oversees IT strategy, risk, budgets and the annual BCP/DR review.
typical_evidence: ITSC terms of reference; membership; minutes for the period
category: RBI IT Governance MD 2023 (now 2026 cyber directions): para 6 (2026 CB: paras 17-18)

title: IT Steering Committee and Head of IT
summary: Senior management sets up an IT Steering Committee of IT and business leaders that meets at least quarterly, and appoints a senior, competent Head of IT accountable for IT execution and controls.
typical_evidence: ITSC charter; Head of IT appointment; steering committee minutes
category: RBI IT Governance MD 2023 (now 2026 cyber directions): paras 7-8

title: IT and information security policies
summary: Board-approved IT, information security and cyber security policies, plus a Cyber Crisis Management Plan, are in place and reviewed by the Board at least annually.
typical_evidence: Approved policies with annual review dates
category: RBI IT Governance MD 2023 (now 2026 cyber directions): paras 5, 24(a)

title: CISO and Information Security Committee
summary: A senior CISO with no reporting line to the Head of IT and no business targets; an Information Security Committee under ITSC oversight manages cyber security; reviews go to the Board or its committees quarterly.
typical_evidence: CISO appointment; reporting line; ISC minutes
category: RBI IT Governance MD 2023 (now 2026 cyber directions): para 24(b)-(d) (2026 CB: paras 27-28)

title: IT asset inventory and classification
summary: Information assets are classified by confidentiality, integrity and availability criticality; end-of-support and AMC dates are tracked, with a technology refresh plan before end of support.
typical_evidence: Asset inventory with criticality and owners
category: RBI IT Governance MD 2023 (now 2026 cyber directions): para 9

title: Capacity management
summary: IT capacity needs are assessed at least annually against peak trends and projected needs; the assessment and remedial measures are reviewed by the ITSC.
typical_evidence: Capacity dashboards; capacity plan
category: RBI IT Governance MD 2023 (now 2026 cyber directions): para 11

title: Change and patch management
summary: Documented change and patch policy: assess business impact, apply changes securely and on time with approvals, document them, and keep a way to recover from failed changes.
typical_evidence: Change records for sampled changes; patch reports
category: RBI IT Governance MD 2023 (now 2026 cyber directions): para 13

title: Audit trails
summary: Critical systems generate audit trails for user and system activity, which are protected, retained and reviewed.
typical_evidence: Audit logging configuration; log retention; review records
category: RBI IT Governance MD 2023 (now 2026 cyber directions): para 15

title: Access control and privileged access
summary: Need-based access under ITSC-approved standards; privileged users closely supervised with activity logged and reviewed; MFA for privileged users of critical systems and for remote access to them.
typical_evidence: Access reviews; PAM configuration; MFA exports
category: RBI IT Governance MD 2023 (now 2026 cyber directions): paras 19-20

title: Cyber security risk assessment and VAPT
summary: Annual IT and cyber risk reviews; critical and customer-facing systems get vulnerability assessment every 6 months and penetration testing every 12 months by independent experts, with findings fixed on a deadline.
typical_evidence: Risk assessment; VAPT reports; remediation tracking
category: RBI IT Governance MD 2023 (now 2026 cyber directions): paras 22, 25-26 (2026 CB: para 151)

title: Security monitoring (SOC)
summary: The CISO's office manages and monitors a Security Operations Centre; an outsourced SOC must meet the outsourcing direction's SOC controls. The 2026 directions add a full SOC chapter.
typical_evidence: SOC contract or setup; monitoring use cases; alert records
category: RBI IT Governance MD 2023 (now 2026 cyber directions): para 24(d) (2026 CB: Chapter VI)

title: Cyber incident response and reporting
summary: Board-approved incident response and recovery policy with classification, root-cause analysis and drills; report cyber incidents to RBI within 6 hours of detection (DAKSH under the 2026 directions) and to CERT-In.
typical_evidence: Incident response plan; reporting procedure; incident reports filed
category: RBI IT Governance MD 2023 (now 2026 cyber directions): para 27 (2026 CB: para 182)

title: Data security
summary: Strong, non-deprecated cryptography for data in transit, processing and authentication; secure storage, transmission and processing controls; no manual changes to data passed between critical applications.
typical_evidence: Data classification policy; encryption settings; DLP
category: RBI IT Governance MD 2023 (now 2026 cyber directions): paras 16-17, 23

title: Business continuity and disaster recovery
summary: Board-approved BCP/DR policy; RTO and RPO for critical systems; DR drills at least half-yearly including a full business day run from DR; backups restored periodically; DC and DR kept in sync.
typical_evidence: BCP and DR policy; DR drill reports; RTO and RPO
category: RBI IT Governance MD 2023 (now 2026 cyber directions): paras 28-29 (2026 CB: para 165)

title: Information systems audit
summary: An IS Audit Policy approved and reviewed annually by the Board's Audit Committee; a separate, skilled IS audit function with risk-based planning; the committee reviews critical IT and cyber issues.
typical_evidence: IS audit policy and plan; IS audit reports; findings tracker
category: RBI IT Governance MD 2023 (now 2026 cyber directions): para 30 (2026 CB: paras 224-227)

title: Board-approved IT outsourcing policy
summary: Regulated entities have a Board-approved policy for outsourcing IT services, including materiality assessment, and remain responsible for outsourced activities.
typical_evidence: Outsourcing policy; materiality assessments
category: RBI IT Outsourcing MD 2023 (now 2025 outsourcing directions): paras 4, 9

title: Due diligence of service providers
summary: Risk-based due diligence before engaging and at renewal, covering capability, financial, operational, legal, reputational and security factors and concentration risk.
typical_evidence: Due diligence records; vendor security assessments
category: RBI IT Outsourcing MD 2023 (now 2025 outsourcing directions): paras 13-14

title: Contract terms
summary: Agreements cover service levels; data confidentiality and security; data location; sub-contracting; incident notification; audit and inspection rights for the RE and RBI; business continuity; termination and exit.
typical_evidence: Contract clause review; for vendors: the RE's outsourcing addendum
category: RBI IT Outsourcing MD 2023 (now 2025 outsourcing directions): paras 15-16

title: Audit and inspection rights for RE and RBI
summary: Service providers give the regulated entity and RBI (or their auditors) access to records, premises and audit reports.
typical_evidence: Contract audit clause; audit reports shared (SOC 2 or ISO certificate)
category: RBI IT Outsourcing MD 2023 (now 2025 outsourcing directions): paras 16, 19(8), 21(3)

title: Incident notification by service provider
summary: Service providers report cyber incidents to the regulated entity without undue delay, so it can report to RBI within 6 hours of the provider detecting them.
typical_evidence: Contract notification clause; incident procedure step to notify RE customers
category: RBI IT Outsourcing MD 2023 (now 2025 outsourcing directions): para 17(8) (2025 CB: para 56)

title: Provider business continuity and exit
summary: Service providers maintain and test BCP and DR; the RE has an exit strategy to move services without disruption.
typical_evidence: Provider BCP test results; exit plan
category: RBI IT Outsourcing MD 2023 (now 2025 outsourcing directions): paras 18, 22

title: Cloud and shared services controls
summary: Cloud adoption policy covering the data lifecycle; risk-assessed provider selection; tenant isolation; RE-controlled keys preferred; role-based access with MFA; provider logs fed to the SOC; cloud exit plan.
typical_evidence: Cloud security configuration; data location; key management
category: RBI IT Outsourcing MD 2023 (now 2025 outsourcing directions): Appendix I

title: Payment system data stored only in India
summary: System providers and their intermediaries store all payment system data (end-to-end transaction details) only in India; a copy of the foreign leg of a cross-border transaction may also be held abroad.
typical_evidence: Data location evidence (cloud regions; database locations) for payment data
category: RBI Payment data storage 2018: para 2(i); FAQs

title: Foreign processing brought back to India
summary: If processed abroad, the data is deleted there and brought back to India within one business day or 24 hours of processing, whichever is earlier.
typical_evidence: Data flow documentation; deletion job evidence for any foreign leg
category: RBI Payment data storage 2018: FAQs (Jun 2019)

title: System audit report on data localisation
summary: A system audit report by a CERT-In empanelled auditor certifying localisation, approved by the Board, is submitted to RBI.
typical_evidence: SAR by a CERT-In empanelled auditor; submission record
category: RBI Payment data storage 2018: para 2(iii)
